implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 was adopted in 2024 and reissued 2026-09-15, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). Procedures for 6-month access reviews and vendor access are being written (STD-06).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider (SOC 2 Type 2); SYS-01 vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); franchisor (SYS-02)
implementation_statement: Corporate, CRO, and resort accounts are created in the identity provider from the HR system feed and federated to SYS-01, the cloud accounts, and email. Hotels 3 to 6 front desk accounts in the brand PMS are requested from the franchisor by each General Manager. Gaps: SYS-01 access reviews are annual (last February 2026), not every 6 months; P07 found brand PMS accounts of former employees still active at 2 of 4 franchised hotels; night auditors at 3 franchised hotels share one login.
evidence: Identity provider export; SYS-01 user and role export; brand PMS user lists; HR termination report

implementation_statement: Account creation, disabling, and removal are automated from the HR system for every identity provider account and the federated SYS-01 and cloud accounts. Brand PMS accounts are outside this automation.
Identity provider accounts inactive for 90 days are disabled automatically. Local accounts on the Resort 2 POS server and lock servers have no inactivity rule.
evidence: Identity provider policy; local account review

implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces 31 role-based permission sets; the identity provider enforces group-based access to cloud accounts and corporate applications.
evidence: SYS-01 role catalog; cloud permission sets

implementation_statement: The resorts separate payment, POS, PMS workstation, door lock, building systems, CCTV, and office traffic into VLANs with firewall rules at the SD-WAN edge. Gaps: Hotels 3 to 6 run one flat staff network behind the brand-managed firewall; Active Directory traffic is allowed between the Resort 2 POS VLAN and the corporate network (P07).
evidence: Firewall rule exports; VLAN design; P07 reachability test

implementation_statement: Folio adjustments, refunds, and rate overrides above set limits need a second approver in SYS-01. Brand PMS limits at Hotels 3 to 6 are set by the franchisor and not reviewed by the company. Corporate payment releases need two approvers in the banking portal.
evidence: SYS-01 approval settings; banking portal roles

implementation_statement: Roles follow job need in SYS-01 and the identity provider. Gap: 46 of 162 SYS-01 users hold the 'view full card number' permission; 8 need it (front office managers and the 2 accounts receivable clerks who process online travel agency virtual cards).
Administrators use separate administrator accounts for administrative work; daily work runs from standard accounts.

Administrator rights for the cloud accounts and SYS-01 are granted just in time through the privileged access broker. Gap: domain administrators at the resorts and local administrators on the Resort 2 POS server and lock servers are standing accounts outside the broker.
evidence: Privileged access broker policy; domain admin group export

implementation_statement: Privileged actions in the cloud accounts, identity provider, and SYS-01 are logged and sent to the SIEM. Privileged use on the Resort 2 POS server and lock servers is logged locally only.
The identity provider locks accounts after repeated failed sign-ins and alerts on password spraying.
PCs lock after 15 minutes of inactivity by group policy. Front desk PCs at Hotels 3 to 6 use a brand image with a 30-minute lock that the company does not control.
evidence: Group policy report; brand image settings

implementation_statement: SYS-01 ends idle sessions after 15 minutes.
evidence: SYS-01 vendor SOC 2 report; configuration screen

implementation_statement: Staff remote access uses the VPN with MFA. Gaps: the Resort 2 POS vendor and lock vendor use their own always-on remote tools without MFA or session approval; the franchisor's network vendor has standing access to the Hotels 3 to 6 firewalls.
evidence: VPN configuration; remote tool inventory; P07 test

implementation_statement: VPN sessions are logged to the SIEM. Vendor remote tool sessions at Resort 2 are not logged or recorded.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: VPN and SD-WAN tunnels use strong encryption (TLS 1.2 or higher, IPsec).

Staff Wi-Fi at the resorts uses enterprise authentication on its own VLAN; guest Wi-Fi is a separate vendor network with client isolation. Gap: no check for unauthorized wireless access points at Hotels 3 to 6.
evidence: Wireless controller configuration; guest Wi-Fi vendor letter

implementation_statement: Company tablets and phones are enrolled in mobile device management with a passcode and remote wipe. Housekeeping tablets at Hotels 3 to 6 are brand-supplied and not enrolled.
Staff may not use personal devices for card data. Use of the franchisor's systems is governed by the franchise agreements, which do not state security terms beyond brand standards.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-01 and POL-05 (2026-09-15). The training procedure is being updated for role-based payment training.
All employees complete annual security awareness training at hire and each year; quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.1%).
Training covers phishing. Gap: front desk and CRO staff get no training on callers who try to obtain guest or card information by phone.
Administrators and security staff get role-based training. Gap: no training on payment device inspection for front desk and outlet staff (Req 9.5.1.3).
Training records are kept in the learning system for 3 years.
Logging requirements are in POL-03. The logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is in draft.
Identity, email, cloud, EDR, and corporate and resort firewall events are logged and sent to the SIEM. Gaps: the Resort 2 POS server, both resort lock servers, and Hotels 3 to 6 do not send logs.
SIEM sources record user, time, event type, source, and outcome. Resort 2 POS application logs lack user IDs for some actions.
The SIEM platform provides storage for 12 months of searchable logs.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The MSSP alerts when a SIEM source stops sending. Sources that were never connected (gap 6) produce no alert.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews alerts 24x7. Gap: logs of CDE components are not reviewed daily, and SYS-01 user activity reports (card displays, profile exports) are not reviewed.
Automated review use cases for SYS-01 card displays and exports and for POS server events are planned with the MSSP (2027-01-31).
Corporate and resort systems synchronize to internal time servers. Resort 2 POS server and lock servers use local clocks.
Cloud and SIEM logs land in a write-once log bucket in the shared services account; only the security team can read it.
SIEM keeps 12 months searchable. Resort 2 POS server and lock servers keep 30 days locally.
evidence: SIEM retention settings; server log settings

implementation_statement: Logging is enabled on connected sources; not on the systems in gap 6.
Assessment and authorization duties are in POL-01. A written procedure for the annual assessment cycle is due 2026-12-31.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses controls each year (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21). The QSA firm supports the 2026 SAQ D.
Assessors are independent: the internal audit firm does not design or run assessed controls and reports to the audit committee.

Interconnections with payment gateways, the booking engine, the channel manager, and the franchisor are covered by contracts. Gap: no written interconnection terms with the franchisor for the brand-managed firewalls and the brand PMS interfaces.
Weaknesses from P03 and P07 are tracked in the POA&M and reported to the audit committee each quarter.
The COO accepted operation of the PMPS with conditions on 2026-09-15 (SSP section 4.2).
Monthly security metrics go to the vCISO; quarterly to the audit committee. The continuous monitoring strategy does not yet cover Hotels 3 to 6.

External penetration test of the resort websites and internet-facing services in 2025. Gaps: no internal penetration test of the CDE and no segmentation test since 2024 (PCI DSS requires segmentation testing at least every 12 months for merchants).
Internal connections (POS to PMS, PMS to locks, PMS to data warehouse) are listed in the interface register. Credentials for 4 of 11 interfaces have not been rotated since installation.
Configuration management requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard (STD-01) is in draft.
Gold images exist for corporate and resort PCs and cloud virtual machines. Gaps: no documented baselines for firewalls, POS workstations, or lock servers; Hotels 3 to 6 use brand images.
Changes to cloud, firewall, and SYS-01 configuration go through tickets with approval. Vendor changes to the Resort 2 POS and lock servers are not ticketed.
Change tickets include a security impact field for cloud and firewall changes; not for website releases by the web agency.
Only the infrastructure team can change cloud and firewall settings. POS and lock vendors change their systems without company approval.

Benchmark settings are applied to corporate and resort PCs and cloud virtual machines. P07 found 3 of 10 sampled servers missing settings and the Resort 2 lock server with the vendor's default administrator password.
Unneeded services are disabled on gold images. The Resort 2 POS server runs remote access services left by the vendor.
Application allowlisting for POS workstations and CRO PCs is planned (2027-03-31) to block memory scrapers and form grabbers.

Asset inventory covers corporate and resort PCs, servers, network devices, and cloud resources. Gaps: no current list of payment devices with serial numbers at Hotels 3 to 6; the inventory is not reconciled to the PCI scope (12.5.1).
The inventory updates automatically for managed endpoints and cloud resources; payment devices and lock hardware are updated by hand.
Users cannot install software on company PCs; requests go through the service desk.
Contingency planning requirements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is in draft.

Recovery priorities and objectives come from the BIA (P05). Gaps: no written recovery procedures for lock servers, the Resort 2 POS server, or the data warehouse; IT sections of hurricane plans exist only at the resorts.

responsible_role: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
implementation_statement: The resort hurricane plans reference the IT recovery order. Hotels 3 to 6 plans do not.
Front desks practice downtime check-in twice a year at the resorts; not at Hotels 3 to 6.
No restore tests of lock servers, the data warehouse, or the CRM have been performed. Quarterly restore tests start 2026-11-10 (POAM-011).
The backup account stores copies in a second region.
Cloud workloads can be rebuilt in a second region; SYS-01 runs on the vendor's platform. Resort on-premises servers have no alternate site.
Dual internet with cellular failover at the resorts and corporate office; single internet at Hotels 3 to 6.

Cloud workloads are backed up daily to the separate backup account with 35-day write-once retention and separate administrator credentials. Gap: resort lock servers are backed up weekly to a local disk only.
Backup reliability tests are planned with the quarterly restore tests.
Cloud workloads can be rebuilt from templates and backups. Lock server and POS server rebuilds depend on vendors and are undocumented.
Identification and authentication rules are in POL-02; the authenticator and privileged access standard (STD-06) is being updated.
Every company-managed account is unique. Gap: night auditors at 3 of 4 franchised hotels share one brand PMS login.
MFA is enforced for all administrators through the identity provider. Gap: Resort 2 POS vendor and lock vendor remote tools have no MFA.
MFA is enforced for all SYS-01 users (since 2025) and all corporate applications. The franchisor enforces MFA for brand PMS users.
Authentication uses replay-resistant protocols (push with number matching, time-based codes).
Identifiers are assigned from HR records and never reused.
Password and MFA rules are set in the identity provider. Gaps: the Resort 2 lock server kept the vendor default administrator password (P07); interface passwords are not rotated.
Identity provider passwords need 14 characters and are checked against a banned list. Local server passwords follow no rule.
Vendor support staff use named accounts in SYS-01 and the cloud. The POS and lock vendor tools use shared vendor logins.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy reissued 2026-09-15.
Security staff and the MSSP are trained. Front office managers and CRO supervisors have not been trained on card compromise steps.
A ransomware tabletop was held in November 2025. No card compromise exercise has been held.
The MSSP triages and contains endpoint threats 24x7; the incident commander runs P08. Gap: card brand and franchisor notice steps were not in the old plan.
The MSSP isolates hosts automatically for high-confidence EDR detections.
Incidents are tracked in the incident log with status and lessons learned.
Notice duties are listed in the P08 notification matrix. Gap: staff did not know the acquirer, Visa, or franchisor clocks.
Incident coordination with the franchisor, SYS-01 vendor, and gateways is in P08. Vendor notice terms are missing from 9 contracts.
The MSSP and the insurer's panel forensic firms provide response assistance.
The P08 runbooks (2026-09-15) cover card compromise and ransomware. They have not yet been tested.
Maintenance on network and server hardware is logged by IT. Vendor maintenance on lock and POS hardware at Resort 2 is not logged.
IT staff perform remote maintenance through the VPN with MFA. Vendor remote maintenance at Resort 2 is always on, unapproved per session, and unrecorded.
Vendor technicians sign in at the resorts. Hotels 3 to 6 keep no visitor log for technicians.
Media protection rules are in POL-04 (2026-09-15).
Printed card forms are being withdrawn. Group sales still prints emailed forms; binders were found unlocked at 1 resort sales office.
Paper with card data must be kept in locked cabinets and destroyed after authorization. Not consistently followed (MP-2).
Paper is shredded by a bonded shredding vendor with certificates; drives are wiped or destroyed with certificates.

responsible_role: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
implementation_statement: Physical security rules are in POL-01 and the facility security standard (STD-10, existing 2024).

responsible_role: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
implementation_statement: Server room and network closet access lists are kept per hotel.

responsible_role: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
implementation_statement: Resort server rooms use badge access. Network closets at Hotels 3 to 6 use keys with no log.

responsible_role: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
implementation_statement: CCTV covers server rooms and front desks at all hotels; recordings kept 30 days.
Resorts keep visitor logs for back-of-house areas; Hotels 3 to 6 do not.
Planning policy is part of POL-01.
This SSP, approved 2026-09-15, documents the PMPS.
All employees acknowledge POL-05 at hire and each year (96% in 2026).
The security architecture for the resorts and cloud is documented in P04. Hotels 3 to 6 architecture is defined by the franchisor and not documented by the company.
The Moderate baseline was selected from the FIPS 199 categorization (section 6).
The baseline was tailored for PCI DSS and the company's risks (section 10.1).

baseline: Program management (not in Moderate baseline; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The security program is documented in POL-01, this SSP, and the roadmap in P03. Standards are being issued.

baseline: Program management (not in Moderate baseline; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The vCISO leads the program and the IT Director is the PCI DSS technical lead, both designated in writing.

baseline: Program management (not in Moderate baseline; selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk appetite and acceptance authority are set in P01 and POL-01.
Personnel security rules are in POL-01 and HR procedures.
Background checks for finance, IT, front office managers, and CRO agents before hire.
Terminations disable identity provider access automatically. Brand PMS removals depend on a request to the franchisor; P07 found 6 of 25 sampled franchised-hotel leavers still active.
evidence: HR termination report; brand user lists

implementation_statement: Transfers trigger a role change in the identity provider; prior SYS-01 roles are not always removed.
Employees sign confidentiality and acceptable use agreements at hire.
Staffing company contracts require background checks for contracted workers; the company does not verify them.
Sanctions for policy violations follow HR discipline procedures.
Risk assessment policy is in POL-01.
The PMPS is categorized Moderate (section 6).
An enterprise risk assessment using NIST SP 800-30 was completed 2026-07-31 (P01); PCI targeted risk analyses are being added.
Supply chain risks are in P01 (R-020 to R-024). Vendor tiering is new (P09).
Quarterly external ASV scans have passed since Q1 2025; internal scans run monthly at the corporate office, CRO, resorts, and cloud. Gap: Hotels 3 to 6 are not scanned.
evidence: ASV reports Q1-Q2 2026; internal scan reports

implementation_statement: Scanner signatures update daily.
Authenticated scans run on Windows systems; the Resort 2 POS server and lock servers are scanned unauthenticated only.
Risk responses are recorded in P01 with owners and dates.
Critical components and processes were identified in the BIA (P05).
Security requirements are added to new contracts from 2026; older contracts lack them.

responsible_role: Vice President of Sales and Marketing
implementation_statement: The resort websites are built by a web agency with no written secure development terms.
The 31 card and guest-data vendors are listed with their PCI responsibilities. Gaps: 9 lack a current AOC or SOC 2 report; no responsibility matrix with the franchisor.
The Resort 2 POS server and lock server run unsupported operating systems. Replacement: POS 2027 Q2; lock server 2027 Q1.
The resort websites sit behind a content delivery service with denial-of-service protection.

SD-WAN edges and resort firewalls deny unsolicited inbound traffic and separate VLANs. Gaps: Hotels 3 to 6 brand-managed firewalls are not visible to the company; Resort 2 POS VLAN allows Active Directory traffic to the corporate network.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Resort firewalls deny by default between VLANs, with documented exceptions. Not verified at Hotels 3 to 6.
Card data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher or P2PE encryption.
Cryptographic protection is applied to all external transmissions of card data.
Keys for cloud storage are managed in the cloud key service; P2PE keys are managed by the solution provider. The company manages no keys for stored card data.
Approved cryptography is used by the providers.
Session tokens are protected by the SaaS providers.
Cloud storage and laptops are encrypted at rest. Gap: card numbers in email and call recordings are readable to anyone with mailbox or recording access (gap 2).
Provider encryption protects stored data; it does not stop authorized users from reading card numbers in emails and recordings.
Corporate and resort PCs and cloud servers are patched monthly; critical patches within 30 days. Gaps: Resort 2 POS server and lock server cannot be patched (unsupported).
EDR runs on 470 of 520 PCs, including CRO PCs. Gaps: 50 PCs at Hotels 3 to 6; Resort 2 POS workstations run a legacy antivirus agent.
The MSSP monitors connected sources 24x7. Gaps: no monitoring of Resort 2 POS, lock servers, or Hotels 3 to 6; no intrusion detection at the CDE perimeter at Resort 2.

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: The MSSP uses automated correlation and analytics on the SIEM.
Outbound traffic from resort VLANs is filtered and logged; Hotels 3 to 6 outbound traffic is not visible.
High-severity alerts reach the Security Manager within 30 minutes (contract).
The Security Manager receives vendor and government advisories and tracks known-exploited vulnerabilities weekly.
EDR detects changes to critical system files on monitored PCs. Gaps: no change-and-tamper detection on the resort website payment pages; no file integrity monitoring on the Resort 2 POS server.
Integrity checks for POS servers and website payment pages are planned (2027-01-31).
Email filtering with link and attachment analysis and spoofing protection (DMARC enforcement).
A records retention schedule is being written (gap 12): guest register 2 years minimum, ID scans check-out plus 30 days, card forms never stored.
A supply chain risk management plan will be part of the vendor risk standard (STD-03, 2026-12-31).
Purchasing requires a security review for new vendors that touch card or guest data (since 2026-01).
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed each year from 2026 (P09). 5 of 12 Tier 1 reviews are complete.
Incident notice terms exist in 22 of 31 card and guest-data vendor contracts.

responsible_role: Resort Directors of Food and Beverage
implementation_statement: P2PE devices have tamper-evident designs; the company inspects them. Brand terminals at Hotels 3 to 6 are inspected informally.

responsible_role: Resort Directors of Food and Beverage
implementation_statement: Resort 1 inspects P2PE devices weekly with a log. Resort 2 and Hotels 3 to 6 inspect informally with no log.
